short_description: Reference iba\app\docs\escalation-304-orphan-justification-review-v1-20260723.md Part A -- 6 orphan configs (not referenced anywhere in iba/app/**/*.py). An "orphan" here means: cfg_setting.key or cfg_enum.name does not appear as a literal string in any .py file under iba/app/, excluding migration/*.py (write-once bootstrap scripts do not count as usage). It seems that the check for usage of a config is inadequate. The check is supposed to confirm that the config is actually used in the application. Usage is defined differently for different types of config. In most cases code will use the config name in the code, to apply the value of the config in the code - so the test is if the value of the config change, will the code automatically respond to it. In other cases, such as governance.* configs must be read by the startup routine explicitly to ensure that AI complies with it; in other cases the config is a lookup, or options, which I assume is not hard coded but uses the config. Validating the use of configs is a method of ensuring that the configs are not ignored in the code, and that a change in config will change the behaviour of the code.

short_description:
GUARDRAIL GAP (found 2026-07-29, IBA app): inactive/deleted flags are not enforced at runtime anywhere in the app -- they are pure metadata read only by configmaint.validate's coherence report. Evidence: cfg_work_package rows set-candidates/build-passages/candidate-quality/candidate-curation/seed-candidate-report all carry inactive=1, yet (a) Cfg.sequence() in iba/app/lib/cfg.py:115 selects from cfg_step by work_package name with no inactive filter; (b) iba/app/run.py never queries cfg_work_package at all -- it dispatches straight from the CLI-supplied package name into cfg.sequence(); (c) Set-Candidates.ps1 only checks _config_loaded()/_data_tables_exist(), not whether its own work package is active. Result: I was about to run Set-Candidates.ps1 -Book Obad (a retired step) and nothing in the app would have stopped it from executing and writing to candidate_seed/span_candidate -- only a manual DB query caught it. The same absence of enforcement likely applies to `deleted`/`inactive` flags on other cfg_* and data tables generally, not just this one work package.

Researcher's required fix (le Roux, 2026-07-29), all three parts, same unit of work:
a) On iba app startup (init.py / Start-Iba.ps1), the FULL config must be read/loaded, not a partial or lazy read -- verify this is actually happening today, not just tables-exist/version checks.
b) No run.py invocation may proceed without checking configs first -- run.py must look up cfg_work_package (and cfg_step) for the requested package/step and refuse (clear error, no partial execution) if inactive=1, before dispatching to any handler.
c) Add a config-level setting/mechanism (e.g. a cfg_setting or a documented convention enforced in a shared helper) that guarantees deleted=1 (and inactive=1) rows are never processed/returned by ANY query across ANY table in the app -- not case-by-case per handler as today (configmaint.py is the only place currently checking inactive, and only for its own validation report).

This is a design/code gap, not a config-content question -- propose the code fix via the normal review path once scoped; do not silently patch it.

short_description: Design gap, 2026-08-17 (widened after researcher pushback in chat: 'it does not make a lot of sense that all progression must go back to a new raise, and reapprove'). Root problem is broader than the original re-assign-to-raised note: reassign_run() accepts 'in-progress' as a valid source state (escalation.py:412) and unconditionally flips it to state='re-assign', with no code path back except Pause (re-assign->on-hold) then Resume (on-hold->raised, escalation.py:478) then a FRESH AnswerRun decision (Approve/Reject/Revise/Hold/Noted). So bouncing an already-decided, mid-work manual item to the other party (e.g. 'can you take a look at this one further') discards its in-progress status entirely -- getting it moving again requires re-approving it from scratch, as if it had never been decided. next_action (still holding the original 'approve') is left stale on the row and never consulted on the way back. Pattern: ANY lateral move (Pause or Reassign) currently forces a full raised-and-redecide cycle to resume forward progress -- there is no 'hand off/park but keep the decision' move. Options for researcher decision, not guessed: (a) Reassign should NOT touch state at all when bouncing an in-progress item -- just change next_action_assigned_to/comment, leaving state='in-progress' so the new assignee can go straight to -Action Complete; (b) give on-hold/re-assign a memory of the state they were parked FROM (a new column, or reuse next_action) so Resume restores in-progress instead of dropping to raised when that's where it came from; (c) leave raised as the sole re-entry point but make AnswerRun cheaper to re-approve (e.g. a -Decision Continue that re-applies the prior next_action without asking the question again). Not fixed in code -- needs your call on which model is right before any of this is built.

All 3 consuming work packages (set-candidates, candidate-curation, candidate-quality) and their steps (candidate.seed/candidate.set/candidate.load/candidate.curate/candidate.validate) remain inactive=1 today, 26 days later -- no 'coming replacement' has landed. handlers/candidate.py still calls cfg_candidate_rule live in its code, but that code is only reachable through the inactive dispatcher steps -- no live path reads it today. cfg_write_grant (configmaint.propose) stays active, deliberately, in case a replacement needs to write it later. Action taken: cfg_table.inactive set to 1 for cfg_candidate_rule (the table's own registration had never been flipped when its data/consumers were in 2026-07-23 -- this closes that gap, per governance.tables 'tables no longer in use must be set as inactive'). Reversible: flip back if the candidate system is ever reactivated.

comment: the entire stream of work around candidates will not be re-activated. the write authority can be withdrawn and the config rule table can be set the inactive
